traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-02-23 (Monday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Tomasz Nowak, Jamie Brennan, David Whitfield, Priya Raman, Hannah Price, Marcus Hale, Callum Reid

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Monday the 23rd. Have we got everybody on?
[00:00:10] Callum Reid: Yeah, morning. The heating in the portakabin has apparently decided it's spring already. Absolutely Baltic in here.
[00:00:17] Jamie Brennan: That's why you've got the coat zipped up to your eyebrows, then.
[00:00:24] Callum Reid: Exactly. Just having a moan, before anyone puts it on a list.
[00:00:31] Priya Raman: Morning. Am I coming through all right? Teams has picked a different microphone again.
[00:00:37] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, you're clear.
[00:00:41] Marcus Hale: Louder than the rest of us, if anything.
[00:00:45] Sarah Okafor: Right, let's get into it. A few things to agree this morning.
[00:00:50] Callum Reid: Just before that, already swapped the filter on the Stretch Wrapper yesterday. That's done.
[00:00:57] Hannah Price: Ah, lovely. I wasn't sure whether that had actually happened.
[00:01:02] Callum Reid: Yeah, all sorted yesterday. Nothing needed on that today.
[00:01:07] Sarah Okafor: Cheers. Whitty, can you send the shift handover report round by the 28th? It matters but it's not urgent.
[00:01:15] David Whitfield: Yeah, so, the report itself? We're not talking about a new format as well?
[00:01:22] Sarah Okafor: No, just send the shift handover report round. No redesign.
[00:01:28] David Whitfield: Fine, I'll send it round by the 28th. Understood, important rather than urgent.
[00:01:34] Jamie Brennan: You looked worried there. Nearly had to choose a font.
[00:01:38] David Whitfield: That's how it starts, mate. Then suddenly you've got twelve tabs.
[00:01:44] Sarah Okafor: Jamie, can you sort the training records for the new starters today? Low priority.
[00:01:50] Jamie Brennan: Today, yeah? Just checking because you said low priority.
[00:01:55] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, still today. Low priority within today, not one to push everything else out for.
[00:02:01] Jamie Brennan: Got you. I'll sort the training records for the new starters today.
[00:02:06] Hannah Price: Yeah, the records side can look tiny until you actually open it.
[00:02:13] Jamie Brennan: Don't say that. I'm choosing to remain optimistic.
[00:02:17] Sarah Okafor: Tommo, can you run the monthly fire alarm test by Wednesday? Not an emergency but don't let it slip.
[00:02:25] Tomasz Nowak: Yep, I'll run the monthly fire alarm test by Wednesday.
[00:02:30] Marcus Hale: Monthly already? Feels like February's only just started.
[00:02:35] Sarah Okafor: I know. But Wednesday's the limit on that one, even though it's not an emergency.
[00:02:42] Tomasz Nowak: Understood. It won't get lost at the bottom.
[00:02:47] Priya Raman: February cheats. Same amount of stuff, fewer days.
[00:02:52] Tomasz Nowak: Doesn't seem to mean fewer meetings, though.
[00:02:56] Tomasz Nowak: While I've got the mic, I'll update the risk assessment for work on the Atlas tomorrow. Normal priority for that.
[00:03:05] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Tommo. Tomorrow, normal priority, agreed.
[00:03:09] Hannah Price: Mm, the wording on those matters. Everyone thinks they mean the same thing until they're stood in front of it.
[00:03:17] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, exactly. Needs to make sense to the person doing the work, not just the person reading it at a desk.
[00:03:25] David Whitfield: Especially when it's a wall of text. You lose the actual risk in all the words.
[00:03:32] Sarah Okafor: Right. There's one more, and this is the one that comes first.
[00:03:37] Sarah Okafor: Tom, can you replace the seals on the GT2 inlet valve today at 2pm? Top priority please.
[00:03:44] Tomasz Nowak: Sorry, you broke up just on the time. Today at two?
[00:03:48] Sarah Okafor: Today at 2pm, yes. Replace the seals on the GT2 inlet valve. Top priority please.
[00:03:54] Marcus Hale: Yeah, that one's the main concern from the plant side.
[00:03:59] Tomasz Nowak: Right, I've got you now. I'll replace the seals on the GT2 inlet valve today at 2pm. That's my top priority.
[00:04:07] David Whitfield: Yeah, makes sense to put that ahead of the paperwork.
[00:04:12] Sarah Okafor: Exactly. The other dates we've agreed still stand, but that gets first call.
[00:04:19] Jamie Brennan: Definitely not going to argue that training records outrank that.
[00:04:25] Tomasz Nowak: Good, because I've only got the one pair of hands, despite popular belief.
[00:04:29] Priya Raman: You were clear that time, by the way. Think it was just a little Teams wobble.
[00:04:37] Hannah Price: Same here. Lost half a second, then it came back.
[00:04:41] Sarah Okafor: Okay. Anything unclear about what we've agreed?
[00:04:46] Hannah Price: No, all clear from me.
[00:04:49] Callum Reid: Same. Nothing else from production this morning.
[00:04:52] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Thanks, everyone. I'll let you get back to it.
[00:04:57] Marcus Hale: Cheers, all.

traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-02-24 (Tuesday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Tomasz Nowak, Jamie Brennan, David Whitfield, Priya Raman, Hannah Price, Marcus Hale

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Tuesday the twenty-fourth. Can you all hear me, or am I talking to myself again?
[00:00:13] Marcus Hale: Bit tinny, but yeah, you're there.
[00:00:17] Priya Raman: Fine this end. Think it's your speaker, Marcus.
[00:00:22] Hannah Price: Before we start, did anyone watch the football last night? Honestly, that last ten minutes.
[00:00:27] David Whitfield: Turned it off. Apparently that was the sensible decision.
[00:00:32] Hannah Price: Wish I had. Sat there arguing with the telly like it could hear me.
[00:00:38] Sarah Okafor: So, much like a Teams call, then.
[00:00:43] Marcus Hale: I'm supposed to be going walking at the weekend. Looking at the weather, it'll be swimming instead.
[00:00:49] Tomasz Nowak: It's only Tuesday. Forecast will change six times.
[00:00:54] Marcus Hale: Yeah, from rain to heavy rain. We've booked somewhere now, anyway.
[00:00:59] Jamie Brennan: Optimistic. Very unlike you.
[00:01:02] Sarah Okafor: Right, before this becomes the weather forecast—Callum Reid's absent today. Everyone else is on.
[00:01:08] David Whitfield: Yep, I'm here. Camera's off, but I am actually here.
[00:01:13] Sarah Okafor: Okay. Updates from yesterday first?
[00:01:16] David Whitfield: Yeah, the shift handover report I was going to send round—can that move to stores Jamie? Jamie, can you take the sending round off me?
[00:01:26] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, I'll take that over from you and send the shift handover report round.
[00:01:33] Sarah Okafor: Fine, thanks both.
[00:01:35] Jamie Brennan: And the new starters' training records, I've sorted those. All fine, that's done.
[00:01:42] Hannah Price: Lovely. Nice to hear 'all fine' for once.
[00:01:46] Jamie Brennan: Tomasz asked me to pass on the monthly fire alarm test as well. That's stuck—the contractor can't get here until it's rescheduled.
[00:01:54] Sarah Okafor: Ah, right. Understood.
[00:01:56] Tomasz Nowak: And, um, I've made a start on the risk assessment update. Got into it, but there's a fair bit left to work through.
[00:02:05] David Whitfield: Always more boxes than space to write in, those forms.
[00:02:10] Tomasz Nowak: Paperwork doesn't have a bypass, unfortunately.
[00:02:14] Sarah Okafor: If only. Anything else before the new stuff?
[00:02:19] Jamie Brennan: Just a finished one: finished the repair on the Water Booster Pump last night. That's sorted.
[00:02:26] Marcus Hale: Lovely. Not the most generous corner for getting your hands into.
[00:02:30] Jamie Brennan: Designed by someone with much smaller knuckles than mine.
[00:02:34] Priya Raman: Oh, and I heard a slight rattle from the long belt. Just an observation, nothing to action yet.
[00:02:43] David Whitfield: Could you hear it over the general racket, or only close up?
[00:02:48] Priya Raman: Only close up. Very faint, no more than that.
[00:02:53] Sarah Okafor: Okay, just an observation for now.
[00:02:56] Tomasz Nowak: Half the trick in there is knowing which rattle you're listening to.
[00:03:02] Sarah Okafor: Right, new work. We need to swap the filter on the CT1 by the end of the week. And that one's safety critical, straight away.
[00:03:13] Marcus Hale: Have we actually got anyone available to take that?
[00:03:17] Tomasz Nowak: I can't take it on, sorry. Haven't got the capacity.
[00:03:21] David Whitfield: No, nor me. Don't want to say yes and then leave it sitting there.
[00:03:26] Priya Raman: I can't pick that one up either.
[00:03:30] Sarah Okafor: Right. It needs doing, but we've got nobody taking it at the moment.
[00:03:35] Jamie Brennan: I can't offer to do that from stores, I'm afraid.
[00:03:41] Sarah Okafor: No, understood. I'm not going to pretend it's covered.
[00:03:46] Marcus Hale: Yeah. That's a gap, then.
[00:03:49] Sarah Okafor: It is. Okay, the other new one.
[00:03:53] Sarah Okafor: Hannah, can you book a contractor to look at the GT2 water valve? Need that booked by tomorrow at 9:30. It matters but it's not urgent.
[00:04:03] Hannah Price: Yeah—sorry, just checking, tomorrow at 9:30 is when you need the booking sorted, not when they need to be standing here?
[00:04:12] Sarah Okafor: Yes, the booking sorted by tomorrow at 9:30. That's the deadline.
[00:04:17] Hannah Price: Fine, I'll book a contractor to look at the GT2 water valve and have the booking sorted by then.
[00:04:25] David Whitfield: Yep, makes sense.
[00:04:27] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Hannah. That's the new work covered in the discussion, then.
[00:04:33] Marcus Hale: Sorry if there's a load of banging coming through. It's the door behind me, not anything exciting.
[00:04:41] Priya Raman: I thought someone was applauding the meeting finishing.
[00:04:45] Marcus Hale: Wouldn't put it past them.
[00:04:48] Sarah Okafor: Cheeky. Right, thanks everyone. We'll leave it there.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-02-25 (Wednesday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Tomasz Nowak, David Whitfield, Hannah Price, Marcus Hale, Callum Reid

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Wednesday the 25th. Can you all hear me?
[00:00:09] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah. Am I coming through all right? Bit noisy this end.
[00:00:14] David Whitfield: You're fine. There's a sort of humming behind you.
[00:00:19] Tomasz Nowak: That's the fan, not me. Haven't had enough coffee to hum.
[00:00:24] Callum Reid: Same. Kettle's taking longer than the shift handover.
[00:00:29] Sarah Okafor: Right, no Jamie Brennan or Priya Raman today. Just us six.
[00:00:34] Hannah Price: Before we get into it, the charity bake sale on Friday — apparently there's proper competition over the brownies.
[00:00:43] Marcus Hale: Competition as in baking them or eating them?
[00:00:48] Hannah Price: Baking. You'd win the other one without much opposition.
[00:00:52] Sarah Okafor: Ha. Anyone got weekend plans that don't involve eating? We were thinking of a walk, but the weather looks grim.
[00:01:00] David Whitfield: A walk to the pub still counts in the rain.
[00:01:05] Callum Reid: Forecast changes every time I open it. I've stopped looking.
[00:01:10] Sarah Okafor: Probably sensible. Right, Tom, how are the bits from the earlier stand-ups going?
[00:01:16] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, so I've made a start on the monthly test.
[00:01:21] Tomasz Nowak: And the seals on the GT2 inlet valve, I'm about halfway through those.
[00:01:27] David Whitfield: Yeah, cheers.
[00:01:28] Hannah Price: The contractor booking for the GT2 Inlet Water Injection Valve is sorted, by the way. All fine.
[00:01:36] Sarah Okafor: Lovely, thanks.
[00:01:39] David Whitfield: And I signed off the inspection on the number two bearing on Tuesday.
[00:01:44] Callum Reid: Tuesday? Sorry, the days are merging a bit.
[00:01:49] David Whitfield: Yeah, yesterday. All signed off.
[00:01:53] Sarah Okafor: Right, onto the new stuff, then.
[00:01:56] Sarah Okafor: I'll run a function test on the pop valve by Thursday.
[00:02:00] Marcus Hale: That's you on the pop valve then, Saz? Sorry, you clipped a bit.
[00:02:06] Sarah Okafor: Yep, me. I'll have the function test done by Thursday.
[00:02:12] Tomasz Nowak: I'll inspect the big valve by the gate for leaks, as well. Tomorrow at 9:30.
[00:02:18] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Tom. Normal priority on that?
[00:02:23] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, normal priority. Tomorrow at 9:30 for the inspection.
[00:02:28] Callum Reid: Tomorrow's Thursday, isn't it? Honestly, ignore me.
[00:02:31] Tomasz Nowak: It is. We could put the days on the kettle for you.
[00:02:37] Sarah Okafor: Cal, can you write up the near miss at the Palletiser?
[00:02:42] Callum Reid: Yeah — when do you need the write-up in?
[00:02:47] Sarah Okafor: On the 3rd, but that one's safety critical, straight away. I need you starting on it now, not waiting till the 3rd.
[00:02:56] Callum Reid: Understood. I'll start straight away and get the near miss at the Palletiser written up on the 3rd.
[00:03:04] Hannah Price: Yeah, not one to leave sitting at the bottom of an inbox.
[00:03:10] Callum Reid: No, absolutely.
[00:03:14] Sarah Okafor: Cheers, Cal.
[00:03:16] Marcus Hale: And I'll do the pre-use checks on the Forklift Fleet tomorrow morning. Normal priority.
[00:03:24] Callum Reid: Sorry, spoke over you there, Marc. You said pre-use checks?
[00:03:29] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'll do the pre-use checks on the Forklift Fleet. Normal priority, tomorrow morning.
[00:03:36] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Marc.
[00:03:39] David Whitfield: Teams just froze on me. Was there something after that?
[00:03:44] Sarah Okafor: No, just me saying thanks to Marc.
[00:03:47] David Whitfield: Right, good. Everyone went very thoughtful for a second.
[00:03:50] Hannah Price: That's just our faces before nine. Mine's thinking about Friday's cake.
[00:03:55] Tomasz Nowak: At least it's for charity. Makes the second slice practically compulsory.
[00:03:59] Callum Reid: That's the sort of technical argument I can support.
[00:04:04] Sarah Okafor: Right, before this becomes a cake meeting — anything else relevant? Nothing more from me.
[00:04:11] David Whitfield: Nothing else here.
[00:04:14] Tomasz Nowak: No, that's me.
[00:04:17] Marcus Hale: All good here too.
[00:04:19] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Thanks, everyone. Catch you on the floor.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-02-26 (Thursday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Tomasz Nowak, David Whitfield, Priya Raman, Hannah Price, Marcus Hale, Callum Reid

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Thursday the twenty-sixth. Can you all hear me?
[00:00:10] Callum Reid: Yeah, although someone's coming through twice.
[00:00:14] Priya Raman: That's me, sorry. Laptop and headset. There, better?
[00:00:17] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Jamie Brennan's absent today, so it's just us.
[00:00:21] Marcus Hale: Before we get serious, there's a birthday cake in the office. Quite a substantial one.
[00:00:27] David Whitfield: Substantial as in enough for everyone, or you've already had a substantial bit?
[00:00:33] Marcus Hale: I'm giving you useful information, David. Don't interrogate the source.
[00:00:39] Hannah Price: He's definitely had some.
[00:00:40] Tomasz Nowak: You can hear the guilt through Teams.
[00:00:45] Sarah Okafor: Right, excellent technical start. Let's have the updates.
[00:00:49] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, I've got a few.
[00:00:52] Tomasz Nowak: The monthly fire alarm test, that's all done.
[00:00:56] Sarah Okafor: Cheers, Tommo.
[00:00:59] Sarah Okafor: And I tested the fire alarm panel yesterday. It's all fine now.
[00:01:04] Priya Raman: Good, that's reassuring.
[00:01:07] Tomasz Nowak: The risk assessment for work on the Atlas is updated as well. All fine.
[00:01:15] Hannah Price: Lovely, thanks.
[00:01:18] Tomasz Nowak: And the seals on the little water valve on two — replaced, that's sorted.
[00:01:25] David Whitfield: Nice one.
[00:01:28] Tomasz Nowak: My leak inspection on the Main Water Isolation Valve has moved. That's now due on the 3rd.
[00:01:36] Sarah Okafor: Okay, thanks, Tom.
[00:01:37] Marcus Hale: Mine's less cheerful. I can't get any further with the pre-use checks; can't get hold of the supplier.
[00:01:46] Callum Reid: Ah, right. That's frustrating.
[00:01:48] Sarah Okafor: One cancellation as well: the filter swap on the tower isn't going ahead now. It's been rolled into next month's shutdown.
[00:01:58] David Whitfield: Understood.
[00:02:01] Marcus Hale: Oh, and just an observation: I saw the pressure on the line 3 barrel dip for a few minutes. It came back on its own.
[00:02:12] Sarah Okafor: Right, just something you noticed?
[00:02:15] Marcus Hale: Yeah, that's all it was.
[00:02:18] Sarah Okafor: Okay. What's new from production, Callum?
[00:02:21] Callum Reid: We've got a jam on the spinner. It needs clearing and the sensors need checking. It's urgent.
[00:02:28] Priya Raman: Sorry, did you say clear it or check the sensors? You broke up halfway through.
[00:02:36] Callum Reid: Both — clear the jam and check the sensors on the spinner.
[00:02:41] David Whitfield: Right, so not just a mechanical clear-out.
[00:02:44] Callum Reid: Exactly, yeah.
[00:02:46] Sarah Okafor: Can anyone take that on?
[00:02:50] Tomasz Nowak: I can't take it, sorry. Haven't got the capacity.
[00:02:53] Priya Raman: Neither can I, I'm afraid.
[00:02:56] Sarah Okafor: Right... no taker for that at the moment, then.
[00:03:00] Sarah Okafor: David, can you schedule downtime for the Atlas with production at half two? That's low priority.
[00:03:06] David Whitfield: Sorry, Sarah, I can't fit that in today. It'll need to be someone else.
[00:03:12] Sarah Okafor: Okay. Haley, can you take that instead — schedule downtime for the Atlas with production at half two? Still low priority.
[00:03:21] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'll schedule downtime for the Atlas with production at half two. Low priority, understood.
[00:03:27] Callum Reid: Sorry, just so I've heard that properly — that's arranging the downtime with production, not starting work on it?
[00:03:35] Sarah Okafor: Yes, just scheduling the downtime.
[00:03:39] Callum Reid: Right, got you. I was talking over the first bit.
[00:03:44] Marcus Hale: Yeah, we're on the same page.
[00:03:47] Sarah Okafor: Anything else for this morning?
[00:03:50] Hannah Price: Nothing from quality to add.
[00:03:52] Priya Raman: No, nothing else from me.
[00:03:55] Tomasz Nowak: That's my lot as well.
[00:03:58] Sarah Okafor: Okay. The spinner is urgent, but we haven't got anyone taking the jam clearance and sensor checks.
[00:04:04] Callum Reid: Yeah. Not the answer I'd hoped for, but understood.
[00:04:09] Marcus Hale: On a slightly brighter note, the cake has proper icing. None of that dry sponge business.
[00:04:15] Hannah Price: That's a very detailed report for someone who hasn't admitted eating it.
[00:04:20] Marcus Hale: No comment.
[00:04:22] Sarah Okafor: Right, on that very convincing note — thanks, everyone.

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-03-02 (Monday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Jamie Brennan, David Whitfield, Priya Raman, Hannah Price, Marcus Hale, Callum Reid

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Monday the second of March. Can you hear me over that fan?
[00:00:08] Marcus Hale: Yeah, you sound like you're calling from inside a tumble dryer, but we can hear you.
[00:00:16] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Professional start, then.
[00:00:19] Jamie Brennan: Before we start, whose new car's that in the car park? The blue one taking up most of the county.
[00:00:28] Callum Reid: Not mine. Mine's the one worth less than the tyres on it.
[00:00:34] David Whitfield: That doesn't narrow it down much.
[00:00:38] Jamie Brennan: Honestly, you need a banksman to get past it.
[00:00:42] Hannah Price: It's parked inside the lines, to be fair.
[00:00:46] Jamie Brennan: Only just. Anyway, very nice. Not jealous at all.
[00:00:50] Sarah Okafor: Right, motoring section finished?
[00:00:52] Priya Raman: Please. Some of us haven't even had a coffee.
[00:00:57] Sarah Okafor: Tomasz Nowak isn't with us today. Everyone else is on, so let's get through the updates first.
[00:01:05] Callum Reid: I'm here, just on the headset. Bit noisy this end.
[00:01:10] Priya Raman: Yeah, you're dipping in and out a bit.
[00:01:14] Callum Reid: Typical. Worked perfectly before I joined.
[00:01:17] Priya Raman: Callum asked me to pass on his near-miss write-up update: he's been working through it, still on it, and it's going fine so far.
[00:01:28] Sarah Okafor: Cheers. I can hear you much better than him, anyway.
[00:01:32] Callum Reid: I heard that bit, funnily enough.
[00:01:35] David Whitfield: Selective headset. We've all had one.
[00:01:39] Sarah Okafor: Go on, then, what have you got?
[00:01:44] David Whitfield: Cal also gave me a message about the other near-miss write-up. He's about halfway through that one.
[00:01:52] Callum Reid: Cheers, mate.
[00:01:55] Sarah Okafor: Right. Quality?
[00:01:57] Hannah Price: Yep, two bits from me.
[00:02:01] Hannah Price: That jam clearance and sensor check from before, the one nobody had taken—I'll take that on.
[00:02:09] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Pricey. That's with you, then.
[00:02:13] Hannah Price: And, um, the less cheerful bit.
[00:02:17] Hannah Price: I can't get any further with inspecting the relief valve for leaks. I need an electrician to isolate it first.
[00:02:24] Priya Raman: Right, understood.
[00:02:26] Sarah Okafor: Okay, thanks for flagging it. What about you, Haley?
[00:02:31] Marcus Hale: Sorry, was muted. Talking away to myself.
[00:02:34] Marcus Hale: The guarding check's all done. Boxed that off.
[00:02:38] Sarah Okafor: Good, cheers.
[00:02:40] Marcus Hale: That's me, really. Short and sweet for once.
[00:02:45] Sarah Okafor: Mine's quick as well: the pressure-drop investigation on the power pack on one is finished, all signed off.
[00:02:54] David Whitfield: Nice. Always good to get a signature at the end of it.
[00:02:59] Sarah Okafor: You had something else, didn't you? Sorry, nearly skipped you.
[00:03:03] David Whitfield: Just a bit of history—the inspection on the long belt, I signed that off on Tuesday. That's already done.
[00:03:11] Sarah Okafor: Ah, yes. Thanks.
[00:03:14] David Whitfield: Tuesday feels about a month ago.
[00:03:18] Callum Reid: Yeah. Right, on the new stuff—
[00:03:21] Callum Reid: I'll do the pre-use checks on the trucks next week.
[00:03:26] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Cal. Not an emergency but don't let it slip.
[00:03:30] Callum Reid: Yep, next week. I've got it.
[00:03:33] Marcus Hale: Sorry, I spoke over the end there. Teams lag.
[00:03:38] Callum Reid: No worries. Think everyone got the important bit.
[00:03:42] Sarah Okafor: They did. Anything new from stores Jamie?
[00:03:47] Jamie Brennan: Yeah so, I'll recalibrate the sensors on the boiler safety valve this afternoon. That's fairly important.
[00:03:53] Sarah Okafor: Agreed, stores Jamie. This afternoon for that.
[00:03:58] Jamie Brennan: Yep, I'll do it.
[00:04:00] Priya Raman: Heard you. You went a bit robotic at the start, but the rest came through.
[00:04:05] Jamie Brennan: That's just my Monday voice.
[00:04:10] Hannah Price: Remarkably similar to your Friday voice.
[00:04:12] Sarah Okafor: Right, unless anyone's being cut off, that's everything for this morning.
[00:04:17] Marcus Hale: All heard here.
[00:04:20] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Thanks, everyone. Cheers.

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".

- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-03-03 (Tuesday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Tomasz Nowak, David Whitfield, Priya Raman, Hannah Price, Marcus Hale

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Tuesday the third. Can you all hear me?
[00:00:10] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, but someone's coming through twice.
[00:00:15] David Whitfield: That'll be me. Laptop and headset both having a go.
[00:00:20] Priya Raman: One of you's quite enough, thanks.
[00:00:22] David Whitfield: There. Constructive feedback as ever.
[00:00:26] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Everyone in?
[00:00:28] Marcus Hale: I'm here, just not on camera. Teams has picked the ceiling again.
[00:00:32] Hannah Price: Very clean ceiling, to be fair.
[00:00:35] David Whitfield: Before we start properly, that charity bake sale on Friday — apparently bought cakes are cheating.
[00:00:41] Tomasz Nowak: Only if you leave the sticker on.
[00:00:45] Priya Raman: That's your entire quality process, is it?
[00:00:48] Sarah Okafor: Right, before this becomes a cake audit. Jamie Brennan and Callum Reid aren't with us today.
[00:00:54] Sarah Okafor: Jamie asked me to pass on that he's about halfway through recalibrating the sensors on the PRV on the boiler.
[00:01:02] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, cheers.
[00:01:04] Sarah Okafor: And Cal's near miss write-up at the palletiser needs to come across to you, Haley. Can you take that over from him?
[00:01:14] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'll take that write-up over from Cal.
[00:01:18] Sarah Okafor: Thanks. Pricey, how have yours gone?
[00:01:21] Hannah Price: Um, the jam and sensor checks — I've got the first half done. Jam's cleared; I haven't got through the sensor checks yet.
[00:01:31] Sarah Okafor: Okay, thanks.
[00:01:33] Hannah Price: And my inspection for leaks is all done, all signed off.
[00:01:39] Tomasz Nowak: Nice one.
[00:01:42] Priya Raman: While we're on finished bits, I finished the repair on the GT2 Number 2 Bearing last night. That's sorted.
[00:01:51] David Whitfield: Ah, lovely. Bet you were pleased to see the back of that.
[00:01:55] Priya Raman: Yeah. Not my favourite evening, put it that way.
[00:02:00] Hannah Price: Only other thing from me, I noticed the big board was running a bit warm on nights, but it settled down. Just an observation.
[00:02:09] Marcus Hale: Was that early on?
[00:02:12] Hannah Price: Yeah, early part of the shift. Nothing ongoing there.
[00:02:16] Sarah Okafor: Right. Two new bits this morning.
[00:02:20] Sarah Okafor: Haley, if you've got a spare minute, can you do a site visit at Kestrel Hydraulics Leeds with the contractor by end of day?
[00:02:30] Marcus Hale: I can't take that, sorry. Can't get away from the plant today.
[00:02:36] Sarah Okafor: No, fair enough. I wasn't sure whether you could get out.
[00:02:42] Marcus Hale: Could you take that one, boss?
[00:02:45] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, I'll do the site visit at Kestrel Hydraulics Leeds with the contractor by end of day, if I've got a spare minute.
[00:02:54] David Whitfield: A spare minute. Those mythical things.
[00:02:57] Sarah Okafor: Exactly. It's not a drop-everything one.
[00:03:00] Tomasz Nowak: Sorry, you clipped there — drop everything?
[00:03:04] Sarah Okafor: Not a drop-everything one. Definitely a 'not' in there.
[00:03:08] Sarah Okafor: Pricey, can you write up the near miss at the wrapper for Monday?
[00:03:14] Hannah Price: Yeah, I'll write up the near miss at the wrapper for Monday.
[00:03:21] David Whitfield: Sorry, I spoke over the end of that.
[00:03:24] Hannah Price: You're all right, I'd finished.
[00:03:27] David Whitfield: Just checking I hadn't drowned you out again. This headset's either nothing or full tannoy.
[00:03:33] Priya Raman: Full tannoy's about right.
[00:03:36] Sarah Okafor: We heard you both. Thanks, Pricey.
[00:03:40] Hannah Price: No worries.
[00:03:41] Sarah Okafor: That's everything I've got. Anything we've missed?
[00:03:45] Tomasz Nowak: Nothing else from me.
[00:03:48] Marcus Hale: No, all good here.
[00:03:51] David Whitfield: Only that I'm feeling personally attacked over the cakes.
[00:03:56] Hannah Price: Nobody actually said you were buying them. Interesting confession, though.
[00:04:00] David Whitfield: Right, I'm saying nothing.
[00:04:03] Sarah Okafor: Probably safest. Cheers, everyone.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Transcript:

[00:00:13] Priya Raman: We can hear you. Bit like you're inside a biscuit tin, but we can hear you.

[00:01:13] Sarah Okafor: My function test on the relief valve is done as well.
[00:01:18] Tomasz Nowak: Good, yeah.

[00:01:27] Callum Reid: Right, lovely.

[00:01:45] Hannah Price: Okay, thanks.

[00:01:56] Hannah Price: Yep, understood.

[00:02:20] Priya Raman: Right, got you.
[00:02:23] Sarah Okafor: Okay, today's work. Three things, and there's a definite order to the production one.
[00:02:28] Callum Reid: Yep. Sorry if there's a racket my end, I'm by the door.

[00:02:55] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, makes sense. No parts, no running.
[00:02:59] Sarah Okafor: Exactly. That collection takes precedence, Reidy.
[00:03:04] Callum Reid: Understood. That one first.
[00:03:06] Sarah Okafor: Priya, can you sort the permit to work and isolation for the big board today? That's fairly important.

[00:04:01] Hannah Price: At least the priorities are clear.

[00:04:20] Jamie Brennan: No, all clear here.
[00:04:23] Priya Raman: Same, yeah.

[00:04:29] Callum Reid: Cheers. And no more football chat, please.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-04-06 (Monday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Priya Raman, David Whitfield, Sarah Okafor, Olumide Adeyemi, Jamie Brennan, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Callum Reid: Morning, all. Can everyone hear me? Teams reckons half of you are still joining.
[00:00:11] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, we're here. It's just thinking about it.
[00:00:15] Sarah Okafor: Before we start, whose new car is that in the car park? Very shiny for this place.
[00:00:24] Jamie Brennan: Someone's new car in the car park and you've already clocked it. Nothing gets past you.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-04-07 (Tuesday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, David Whitfield, Sarah Okafor, Olumide Adeyemi, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Callum Reid: Morning. Can everyone hear me, or am I talking to myself again?
[00:00:08] Marcus Hale: Yeah, got you. The heating in the portakabin, honestly—it's either Arctic or tropical. No middle setting.
[00:00:16] Sarah Okafor: You've still got your coat on, though.
[00:00:19] Marcus Hale: Insurance, that is. Don't trust it.
[00:00:22] Callum Reid: Like the defending in the football last night. Absolutely no confidence in any of it.
[00:00:29] David Whitfield: We doing football analysis or a stand-up, then?
[00:00:34] Callum Reid: All right, all right. Tough audience this morning.
[00:00:38] Hannah Price: Sorry, was that me crackling? I've changed headsets.
[00:00:43] Olumide Adeyemi: You're clear now. Bit loud, if anything.
[00:00:47] Callum Reid: Right. Priya Raman and Jamie Brennan aren't with us today. Sarah, how was overnight?
[00:00:52] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, so, finished the repair on the pump in the pit last night. That's all sorted.
[00:00:59] David Whitfield: Lovely. Not the nicest spot to spend your evening.
[00:01:04] Sarah Okafor: No. Definitely not getting a five-star review.
[00:01:08] Callum Reid: Okay, quick round on the bits from yesterday, then today's work.
[00:01:12] Olumide Adeyemi: Han asked me to pass on where she's got to with the near-miss write-up. She's had a first look, nothing major so far; she's partway through it.
[00:01:23] Hannah Price: Cheers. Wasn't sure I'd get this headset working in time.
[00:01:28] Marcus Hale: And Whitty asked me to say the function test on the HV board is all done.
[00:01:36] Callum Reid: Good, thanks.
[00:01:38] Callum Reid: Mine—the permit to work and isolation for the GT1 fuel valve—that's sorted. All fine.
[00:01:44] Sarah Okafor: Haley asked me to flag the site visit with the contractor. Can't go ahead because the parts haven't turned up.
[00:01:51] Marcus Hale: Yeah. Frustrating, that.
[00:01:53] Callum Reid: Right, onto what we need to agree today.
[00:01:57] Callum Reid: Davey, can you chase the purchase order for the Line 2 Safety Guard Interlock this morning, whenever you get a chance?
[00:02:06] David Whitfield: Yeah—just the purchase order you're after, not chasing a delivery date as well?
[00:02:12] Callum Reid: Just the purchase order, yeah.
[00:02:15] David Whitfield: Okay, I'll chase that this morning, whenever I get a chance.
[00:02:20] Sarah Okafor: This morning's going to disappear quickly, isn't it?
[00:02:23] Callum Reid: Usually does. There's the production downtime slot to pin down as well.
[00:02:29] Callum Reid: I'll schedule downtime for the little water valve on two with production, at half two. Normal priority, that one.
[00:02:38] Sarah Okafor: Okay, Reidy. Better having an actual slot than trying to squeeze it in.
[00:02:44] Marcus Hale: The famous five-minute stop that isn't five minutes.
[00:02:49] Callum Reid: Exactly. None of that.
[00:02:52] David Whitfield: I'll update the risk assessment for work on the GT2 Inlet Water Injection Valve, due tomorrow at 9:30. That's holding production up so it needs doing first.
[00:03:02] Callum Reid: Agreed, Davey. That risk assessment comes first.
[00:03:05] David Whitfield: Yeah, I'll put that ahead of the other bits.
[00:03:09] Olumide Adeyemi: Get the paperwork right before everyone gets carried away, basically.
[00:03:14] Sarah Okafor: Absolutely. No sense rushing past that.
[00:03:16] Callum Reid: Anything else on your side, then?
[00:03:21] David Whitfield: Yeah, I'll clear the jam and check the sensors on the long belt by 11am. Not an emergency but don't let it slip—that's how I'm treating it.
[00:03:31] Marcus Hale: The sensors as well, not just pull the jam out and call it good?
[00:03:36] David Whitfield: Yeah, both. Clear it and check the sensors, by 11am.
[00:03:42] Callum Reid: Right, David Whitfield for that one. Your full name's finally appeared properly on Teams.
[00:03:49] David Whitfield: Sounds like I'm being called into the head's office.
[00:03:54] Hannah Price: Only if he uses your middle name.
[00:03:58] Sarah Okafor: Sorry, talking over you—you're happy with that order of work?
[00:04:02] David Whitfield: Yeah. Risk assessment first, and the belt by 11am. The purchase-order chase fits round those this morning.
[00:04:08] Callum Reid: Okay, that works.
[00:04:10] Hannah Price: Only other thing from me: I heard a slight rattle from the counterbalances. Nothing to action yet, just an observation.
[00:04:19] Marcus Hale: Hard to hear yourself think round there sometimes.
[00:04:24] Hannah Price: Mm. It was only slight.
[00:04:27] Callum Reid: Right. Anything else anyone needs in the room before we break?
[00:04:31] Sarah Okafor: Nothing else from me.
[00:04:34] Marcus Hale: No, that's me. Back to the portakabin climate lottery.
[00:04:38] Olumide Adeyemi: All good here.
[00:04:40] Callum Reid: Lovely. Thanks, everyone. Catch you on the floor.
[00:04:44] David Whitfield: Cheers, all.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-04-08 (Wednesday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Priya Raman, David Whitfield, Sarah Okafor, Olumide Adeyemi, Jamie Brennan, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Callum Reid: Morning, all. Everyone on? Right, let's get going.
[00:00:08] Sarah Okafor: I'm here. Still no coffee, though. That broken coffee machine in the canteen is properly testing my patience.
[00:00:15] Jamie Brennan: Probably doing your blood pressure a favour.
[00:00:20] Sarah Okafor: You'd think. Having the opposite effect, actually.
[00:00:23] David Whitfield: I'm just hoping the weather sorts itself out for the weekend. Supposed to be going camping.
[00:00:31] Marcus Hale: In April? Brave.
[00:00:34] David Whitfield: Yeah, that's one word for it. Forecast changes every time I look.
[00:00:40] Callum Reid: Right, before we get the full shipping forecast, quick round of where we're at.
[00:00:46] Priya Raman: Yep. Tested the relief valve yesterday and it's all fine now. That's sorted.
[00:00:51] Callum Reid: Lovely, cheers.
[00:00:55] Jamie Brennan: I've swapped the filter on the power pack on one as well. All done.
[00:01:02] Olumide Adeyemi: Nice one.
[00:01:04] Marcus Hale: And my visit to Tollgate with the contractor, that's done. All signed off.
[00:01:10] Callum Reid: Good, thanks.
[00:01:12] Callum Reid: I've got the downtime for the little water valve on two agreed with production. Scheduling's sorted.
[00:01:19] David Whitfield: On the risk assessment for the little water valve on two, I've got the first half done. Working through the rest of it.
[00:01:29] Priya Raman: Yep, with you.
[00:01:32] David Whitfield: The jam clearance and sensor checks on the Main Outfeed Conveyor, though—I can't get on with those. Waiting on the permit to be signed.
[00:01:43] Callum Reid: Ah, right. Understood.
[00:01:45] Sarah Okafor: Pricey asked me to pass on that the near-miss write-up for the door switch on two is about halfway through.
[00:01:55] Hannah Price: Cheers. Sorry, was fighting the mute button there.
[00:01:59] Callum Reid: You're coming through now. Right, new stuff this morning.
[00:02:04] Marcus Hale: We've got a pressure drop on the Boiler Feedwater Pump. That's the main thing from my end.
[00:02:10] Callum Reid: Hannah, can you investigate the pressure drop on the Boiler Feedwater Pump? Drop everything for that one.
[00:02:18] Hannah Price: Yeah, I'll investigate it. Understood on the urgency.
[00:02:23] Olumide Adeyemi: Sorry, you clipped out for me. Which pump was that?
[00:02:27] Callum Reid: Boiler Feedwater Pump. Hannah's taking the pressure-drop investigation.
[00:02:31] Hannah Price: Yep, that's mine. Everything else aside for that one.
[00:02:35] Callum Reid: Thanks.
[00:02:38] David Whitfield: While we're on pressure—just an observation—I saw the pressure on the Stretch Wrapper dip for a few minutes. Came back on its own.
[00:02:46] Marcus Hale: Oh, it recovered by itself?
[00:02:49] David Whitfield: Yeah. Nothing outstanding from that, just what I saw.
[00:02:53] Callum Reid: Okay, cheers for the heads-up.
[00:02:55] Sarah Okafor: I'll recalibrate the sensors on the heater box on one at half two.
[00:03:02] Olumide Adeyemi: Half two, boss? Sorry, someone was talking outside here.
[00:03:08] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, at half two.
[00:03:10] Priya Raman: I heard half two as well. Not just your headset this time.
[00:03:16] Callum Reid: And I'll sort the permit to work and isolation for the line 2 guard for Monday.
[00:03:22] Sarah Okafor: Monday for that, Reidy?
[00:03:25] Callum Reid: Yeah, Monday. That's holding production up so it needs doing first.
[00:03:31] Marcus Hale: Right, got you.
[00:03:34] Jamie Brennan: There's also the purchase order for the IM1 hydraulic unit that needs chasing.
[00:03:41] Sarah Okafor: I'll chase the purchase order for the IM1 hydraulic unit tomorrow. Normal priority.
[00:03:48] Jamie Brennan: Cheers, Saz.
[00:03:50] Sarah Okafor: No worries. At least I can read that one on my screen without squinting.
[00:03:56] Jamie Brennan: That's because I've finally made the font bigger.
[00:04:00] Callum Reid: A genuine improvement, then. Anything else new we need in this morning?
[00:04:05] Olumide Adeyemi: Nothing else from me, no.
[00:04:08] Priya Raman: No, that's me as well.
[00:04:10] Hannah Price: All clear here. I can hear everyone now, at least.
[00:04:15] Marcus Hale: Nothing more from my side.
[00:04:18] David Whitfield: Nor mine. I'll spare you the rest of the forecast.
[00:04:23] Callum Reid: Much appreciated. Right, thanks everyone. Leave it there.
[00:04:26] Sarah Okafor: Cheers, all.

summary.description: Short imperative description of the job being talked about.

speaker.description: Display name of the person who said it, exactly as in the transcript.

owner_mention.description: Whose job it is, as named ('I'll' = the speaker; 'Dave asked me to say' = Dave). Null if not said.

new_owner_mention.description: reassigned only: who takes the job over or picks it up.

component_mention.description: Equipment exactly as people referred to it; resolve 'it'. Null if none.

site_mention.description: Off-site location, as said. Null if none.

due_mention.description: Deadline words as spoken. Null if none.

due_date.description: Deadline as YYYY-MM-DD using the meeting date and the date rules. Null if none.

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.
