traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-04-09 (Thursday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Priya Raman, David Whitfield, Sarah Okafor, Olumide Adeyemi, Jamie Brennan, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Callum Reid: Morning, everyone. Right, Thursday. Everyone awake, more or less?
[00:00:10] Jamie Brennan: More or less. Whose new car is that in the car park? The shiny one taking up about a space and a half.
[00:00:20] David Whitfield: Not mine. Mine's the one with more mud than paint.
[00:00:25] Jamie Brennan: Looks like it's only just come out of the showroom. Brave bringing it here.
[00:00:31] Sarah Okafor: Give it a week. It'll match the rest.
[00:00:34] Callum Reid: Right, car reviews later. Think we've got all eight of us.
[00:00:40] Priya Raman: Can you hear me? Teams has picked the wrong microphone again.
[00:00:46] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, you're coming through. Bit hollow, but we can hear you.
[00:00:52] Priya Raman: That's probably just me, then.
[00:00:56] Callum Reid: Ha. Marc, anything from last night before we get into the updates?
[00:01:02] Marcus Hale: Yeah, finished the repair on the pop valve last night. That's sorted.
[00:01:06] David Whitfield: Ah, good stuff.
[00:01:10] Callum Reid: Cheers. Dave, where are you with yours?
[00:01:13] David Whitfield: The pressure-drop investigation, I've boxed that off. All done.
[00:01:18] Callum Reid: Good, thanks.
[00:01:20] David Whitfield: And I'm not chasing that purchase order now. The other shift already sorted it, so that chase is cancelled.
[00:01:28] Jamie Brennan: Fair enough. No point two shifts doing the same chase.
[00:01:33] Callum Reid: Exactly. Hannah, how about you?
[00:01:36] Hannah Price: Um, the near-miss write-up's blocked. Waiting on the permit to be signed, so I can't take it any further.
[00:01:44] Sarah Okafor: Right. Frustrating, that.
[00:01:47] Hannah Price: Yeah. On my pressure-drop investigation, I've done the prep; just the write-up left.
[00:01:54] Callum Reid: Okay, cheers.
[00:01:56] Marcus Hale: Saz asked me to pass on the sensor recalibration on the line 1 mould temp. She's still on it, going fine so far.
[00:02:06] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Marc. Wasn't sure I'd get on the call when we spoke.
[00:02:12] Sarah Okafor: And my purchase-order chase is done. All signed off.
[00:02:17] Callum Reid: Lovely. Right, today's new bits, then.
[00:02:21] Callum Reid: Hannah Price, can you swap the filter on the cooling tower at half two? No rush.
[00:02:27] Hannah Price: Yeah, I'll swap it at half two.
[00:02:30] Callum Reid: Cheers. It's not an urgent one.
[00:02:34] Hannah Price: Yep, that's fine with me.
[00:02:36] Priya Raman: Sorry, I talked over the end there. Only said okay.
[00:02:41] Callum Reid: No worries. I'll organise the toolbox talk for the team by 11am. No rush on that either.
[00:02:48] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Cal. Happy with that.
[00:02:51] Callum Reid: Nothing elaborate, just a toolbox talk.
[00:02:55] Jamie Brennan: So not forty slides and a motivational video?
[00:03:00] Callum Reid: You've ruined the surprise now.
[00:03:04] Marcus Hale: Yeah, so I'll sort the training records for the new starters as well. No rush on those.
[00:03:10] Sarah Okafor: Cheers, Marc.
[00:03:13] Marcus Hale: Honestly, feels like there's more paperwork to being new than actually being new.
[00:03:18] Hannah Price: You stop being new just as you learn where everything lives.
[00:03:23] Callum Reid: Sounds about right. Mide, you were about to come in?
[00:03:29] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah. I'll go to the sub to pick up the replacement parts for the counterbalances after lunch.
[00:03:35] Callum Reid: Thanks, Mide. Top priority please, that one.
[00:03:39] Olumide Adeyemi: Understood. I'll make that my top priority after lunch.
[00:03:44] Jamie Brennan: Actual parts collection, not your scenic tour past the coffee machine.
[00:03:48] Olumide Adeyemi: One time, Jamie. You've had about six months out of that.
[00:03:53] Priya Raman: That's pretty good value for a coffee, to be fair.
[00:03:58] Callum Reid: Right, before this becomes a full review of everyone's breaks—any other new work to raise?
[00:04:06] David Whitfield: Nothing else from me.
[00:04:08] Priya Raman: No, nothing from electrical.
[00:04:10] Hannah Price: Nothing else here.
[00:04:12] Sarah Okafor: No more from me either. All clear on what's been agreed.
[00:04:18] Callum Reid: Okay, that's everyone, then.
[00:04:20] Jamie Brennan: Still reckon that car belongs to a visitor. Nobody here keeps anything that clean.
[00:04:26] David Whitfield: Speak for yourself. I washed mine. Once.
[00:04:30] Callum Reid: On that impressive note, we'll leave it there. Cheers, everyone.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-04-10 (Friday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Priya Raman, David Whitfield, Olumide Adeyemi, Jamie Brennan, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Callum Reid: Morning, everyone. Friday at last. Can you all hear me?
[00:00:07] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, bit tinny, but you're there.
[00:00:10] David Whitfield: Unfortunately, yes.
[00:00:12] Callum Reid: Lovely. Whose new car's that in the car park, then? Taking up about a space and a half.
[00:00:20] Jamie Brennan: Not mine. Mine's the one worth less than the tyres on that.
[00:00:26] Hannah Price: It's parked diagonally for extra prestige.
[00:00:28] Priya Raman: Never mind the car, the heating in the portakabin's absolutely roasting. I've got the window open in April.
[00:00:36] Olumide Adeyemi: You've found the only warm bit of the factory.
[00:00:39] Priya Raman: Yeah, apparently all the heat's been allocated to my chair.
[00:00:44] Callum Reid: Right, before we get into heating policy. Marcus Hale and Sarah Okafor aren't with us today. Dave, how are you getting on?
[00:00:53] David Whitfield: Yeah, so the risk assessment for work on the GT2 Inlet Water Injection Valve, I've updated that. All done.
[00:01:02] Callum Reid: Good, cheers.
[00:01:04] David Whitfield: And CV01, jam's cleared and I've checked the sensors. All fine, that's sorted.
[00:01:10] Priya Raman: Ah, good.
[00:01:12] David Whitfield: Only other thing from me, I heard a slight rattle from the Main Water Isolation Valve. Nothing to action yet, just an observation.
[00:01:21] Callum Reid: Okay, understood. Hannah?
[00:01:24] Hannah Price: The pressure-drop investigation, I'm still on it. Got a bit further with it, going fine so far.
[00:01:30] Callum Reid: Thanks. Olu, you had an update as well?
[00:01:35] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, the replacement parts from Northfield. Went over, picked them up, all done. No issues found.
[00:01:41] Jamie Brennan: Nice. An uneventful parts run, for once.
[00:01:46] Callum Reid: And I've made a start on organising the toolbox talk for the team. That's ticking along.
[00:01:53] Priya Raman: Okay, cheers.
[00:01:56] Callum Reid: One from the boss, in her absence: the sensor recalibration on the heater box on one is moving over to Hannah Price. Hannah, you okay taking that over?
[00:02:07] Hannah Price: Yeah, I'll take over that recalibration.
[00:02:09] Callum Reid: Thanks. Right, today's new bits.
[00:02:11] Callum Reid: First, stores Jamie, can you sort the permit to work and isolation for the pick and place on two? That one's safety critical, straight away.
[00:02:22] Jamie Brennan: Yeah. You mean sorting both the permit and the isolation, not just the paperwork?
[00:02:28] Callum Reid: Both, yeah. That's the immediate one.
[00:02:32] Jamie Brennan: Understood, I'll sort the permit to work and isolation for the pick and place on two straight away.
[00:02:41] Priya Raman: Yeah, sensible. No ambiguity on that one.
[00:02:45] Callum Reid: Exactly.
[00:02:48] Jamie Brennan: Okay, I'm with you. What else have you got for me?
[00:02:54] Callum Reid: Jamie, can you go to Kestrel in Leeds to pick up the replacement parts for the feed pump after lunch? That's holding production up so it needs doing first.
[00:03:06] Jamie Brennan: Yep, I'll go to Kestrel in Leeds after lunch and pick up the replacement parts for the feed pump.
[00:03:15] David Whitfield: Yeah, that's the production hold-up at the minute.
[00:03:19] Olumide Adeyemi: Sorry, first as in before the—
[00:03:24] Callum Reid: No, sorry, talking over you. Safety one straight away. After lunch, the parts run needs doing first because production's waiting on it.
[00:03:32] Jamie Brennan: Got you. Immediate safety bit, then the collection first after lunch.
[00:03:38] Hannah Price: Friday in Leeds. Living the dream, Jamie.
[00:03:42] Jamie Brennan: Oh, absolutely. All the glamour ends up in stores.
[00:03:47] Callum Reid: Last one, stores Jamie: can you do the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the little water valve on two for Monday? Top priority please.
[00:03:57] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, I'll do the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the little water valve on two for Monday. Top priority, understood.
[00:04:05] Priya Raman: Sorry, was that Monday? Your audio clipped.
[00:04:09] Callum Reid: Monday, yes.
[00:04:12] Jamie Brennan: That's clear. Three for me, then.
[00:04:16] Callum Reid: Yep, those three.
[00:04:20] Olumide Adeyemi: Audio's gone a bit underwater again.
[00:04:24] David Whitfield: Might just be how we sound by Friday.
[00:04:29] Priya Raman: No, definitely Teams. Though I wouldn't rule it out.
[00:04:34] Callum Reid: Right, we'll leave it there before I turn into a submarine.
[00:04:38] Hannah Price: Cheers, everyone.
[00:04:40] Jamie Brennan: Cheers.
[00:04:43] Callum Reid: Thanks all. Bye.

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-04-13 (Monday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Priya Raman, David Whitfield, Sarah Okafor, Olumide Adeyemi, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Callum Reid: Morning, everyone. Monday the thirteenth. You all hearing me?
[00:00:09] David Whitfield: Yep. Bit tinny, but that's probably this headset.
[00:00:15] Olumide Adeyemi: You're coming through fine here.
[00:00:17] Callum Reid: Right, lovely. Everyone survived the weekend, then?
[00:00:20] Marcus Hale: More importantly, there's a birthday cake in the office. Proper big one.
[00:00:26] Sarah Okafor: Whose birthday?
[00:00:29] Marcus Hale: Didn't get that far. Saw the cake, thought you'd want the important information.
[00:00:35] Hannah Price: Excellent investigation, that.
[00:00:38] Priya Raman: Has it actually got a name on it?
[00:00:42] Marcus Hale: Probably under the bit that's missing.
[00:00:45] Callum Reid: Right, before this becomes cake forensics, Jamie Brennan's absent today. We've got everyone else on.
[00:00:51] Hannah Price: Yeah. Shall I start with mine?
[00:00:56] Hannah Price: The near-miss write-up — I've had a first look, nothing major so far. Only at the initial notes stage, though.
[00:01:05] Callum Reid: Okay, cheers.
[00:01:07] David Whitfield: Hannah asked me to pass on the pressure-drop investigation. That's cancelled our end; the supplier's doing it under warranty instead.
[00:01:16] Callum Reid: Fair enough, makes sense.
[00:01:19] Hannah Price: And recalibrating the sensors on the heater box on one has moved to next week. That's the new deadline for mine.
[00:01:27] Callum Reid: Yep, understood.
[00:01:29] Sarah Okafor: Pricey asked me to mention the filter swap on CT1 as well. She's had a first look, nothing major so far, but hasn't got as far as the swap yet.
[00:01:40] David Whitfield: Mm, okay.
[00:01:43] Sarah Okafor: And I already swapped the filter on the chiller on three yesterday. That one's sorted.
[00:01:50] David Whitfield: Ah, good. Lovely when they actually come out without a fight.
[00:01:56] Marcus Hale: On my training records for the new starters, I've done the prep. Just the write-up left now.
[00:02:02] Callum Reid: Thanks. Um, one handover from me as well.
[00:02:06] Callum Reid: Organising the toolbox talk for the team — I'm handing that over to Olumide Adeyemi. Can you take that from me?
[00:02:14] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, I'll take over organising the toolbox talk.
[00:02:18] Callum Reid: Cheers. Right, today's new bits. What's happening on two?
[00:02:23] Sarah Okafor: The line 2 robot's jammed. Production's held up on that at the minute.
[00:02:28] Callum Reid: Is it just the jam, or are the sensors involved as well?
[00:02:34] Sarah Okafor: Can't call the sensors good yet. It needs clearing and those checking, not just pulling the jam out and assuming.
[00:02:43] David Whitfield: Yeah, a clear gap isn't necessarily a happy sensor.
[00:02:47] Sarah Okafor: I'll clear the jam and check the sensors on the line 2 robot by tomorrow morning. That's holding production up so it needs doing first.
[00:02:57] Callum Reid: Thanks, Saz. That's yours, then.
[00:03:00] Sarah Okafor: Yep, I'll take it.
[00:03:02] Callum Reid: Mide, can you take vibration readings on the hot bearing by Monday? Drop everything for that one.
[00:03:08] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, I'll take the vibration readings on the hot bearing.
[00:03:12] Olumide Adeyemi: Monday as in today, yeah? Just checking, not trying to buy myself a week.
[00:03:18] Callum Reid: Today, yes. Definitely not next Monday.
[00:03:22] David Whitfield: Worth a try, though.
[00:03:25] Olumide Adeyemi: Ha. No, understood — that one takes priority for me.
[00:03:29] Priya Raman: And I'll run the monthly fire alarm test on Friday.
[00:03:34] Callum Reid: Thanks, Pri. Agreed.
[00:03:37] Marcus Hale: Friday's getting a theme. Isn't that cake day as well?
[00:03:41] Priya Raman: The charity bake sale on Friday, yeah. Nothing engineering-related about that, before anyone starts.
[00:03:47] Hannah Price: Depends how your sponge turns out.
[00:03:49] Priya Raman: Oi. Structurally sound, mine.
[00:03:53] Callum Reid: All right, any other observations before we finish?
[00:03:57] Marcus Hale: Only that I heard a slight rattle from the Atlas. Nothing to action yet, just an observation.
[00:04:05] Callum Reid: Okay, noted. No action off that.
[00:04:09] Marcus Hale: Sorry, did I clip out halfway through? Teams went a bit funny.
[00:04:14] Olumide Adeyemi: No, we got you. Your picture froze, voice was fine.
[00:04:19] Marcus Hale: Probably an improvement, the frozen picture.
[00:04:23] Sarah Okafor: Wouldn't like to comment.
[00:04:25] Callum Reid: Very diplomatic. Right, that's us. Thanks, everyone.
[00:04:29] Priya Raman: Cheers, all.
[00:04:31] David Whitfield: Cheers.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

[00:02:59] Jamie Brennan: Right, on the 3rd. Got you.

[00:03:37] Sarah Okafor: It's either the radio or Teams. Never both behaving.

[00:03:47] Callum Reid: Anything else for this morning?

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.
traces.input:
Meeting date: 2026-04-15 (Wednesday)
Attendees: Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Priya Raman, David Whitfield, Sarah Okafor, Olumide Adeyemi, Jamie Brennan, Hannah Price

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Callum Reid: Morning, everyone. All eight of us on? Right, lovely.
[00:00:08] Sarah Okafor: Before we start, there's a birthday cake in the office. Quite a substantial one.
[00:00:15] David Whitfield: Whose birthday is it?
[00:00:18] Sarah Okafor: Couldn't tell you. I got as far as seeing the cake.
[00:00:23] Jamie Brennan: Excellent traceability there.
[00:00:25] Hannah Price: Don't bring quality into it. I'm having a slice regardless.
[00:00:30] Marcus Hale: Am I coming through? I've got you all sounding like you're underwater.
[00:00:34] Olumide Adeyemi: You're clear our end. Is that your headset again?
[00:00:39] Marcus Hale: Yeah, there we go. Better now.
[00:00:43] Callum Reid: Right, quick round of the carry-overs first.
[00:00:46] Jamie Brennan: Callum Reid asked me to pass this one on: the permit to work and isolation for the line 2 guard are now due on the 3rd.
[00:00:56] Callum Reid: Cheers, yes.
[00:00:58] Priya Raman: And stores Jamie asked me to say the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the little water valve on two is all done.
[00:01:08] Jamie Brennan: Thanks, Priya. Had that written down somewhere under my keyboard.
[00:01:12] Hannah Price: My filter swap on the tower is sorted. All done.
[00:01:17] David Whitfield: Nice one.
[00:01:20] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, and mine's sorted as well—the jam's cleared and I've checked the sensors. All finished.
[00:01:26] Callum Reid: Lovely, thanks.
[00:01:28] Callum Reid: I got over to Harbour Road and picked up the replacement parts for the stacker. That one's boxed off.
[00:01:36] Jamie Brennan: Was the traffic as grim as usual?
[00:01:40] Callum Reid: Oh, absolutely. Plenty of time to admire the same set of lights.
[00:01:47] Marcus Hale: Scenic route. Without the scenery.
[00:01:50] Callum Reid: Pretty much. Also, the function test on the heater box on one is finished, all signed off.
[00:01:57] Priya Raman: Lovely.
[00:01:59] Olumide Adeyemi: And just so you're aware, I already swapped the filter on the air compressor yesterday. That's done.
[00:02:07] Callum Reid: Cheers.
[00:02:09] Hannah Price: Only other thing from my walk through: saw the pressure on the barrel on three dip for a few minutes. It came back on its own. Just an observation.
[00:02:21] David Whitfield: Sorry, I talked over the end of that.
[00:02:25] Hannah Price: No, you're all right. That was all.
[00:02:28] Callum Reid: Okay. New bits for today, then.
[00:02:31] Callum Reid: Marcus Hale, can you inspect the feedwater pump for leaks, please?
[00:02:36] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'll inspect the feedwater pump for leaks.
[00:02:41] Callum Reid: Ta.
[00:02:43] Marcus Hale: Sorry, heard my name and Teams froze for a second. Got the actual request, though.
[00:02:50] Olumide Adeyemi: It's picking its moments this morning.
[00:02:54] Callum Reid: Always does. Guarding next—
[00:02:56] Hannah Price: Yeah, I'll check the guarding on the Engel by 11am. That one's safety critical, straight away.
[00:03:03] Sarah Okafor: Yes, absolutely. No argument there.
[00:03:05] Callum Reid: Thanks. Hannah Price on the guarding, then.
[00:03:09] Hannah Price: Yep.
[00:03:11] David Whitfield: Sorry, was that eleven you said?
[00:03:15] Hannah Price: By 11am, yeah. I'm starting straight away.
[00:03:19] David Whitfield: Got you. Audio's a bit woolly this end.
[00:03:23] Priya Raman: You're not the only one. Comes and goes.
[00:03:27] Callum Reid: And stores?
[00:03:30] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, I'll order spare parts for the BFP. Low priority, that one.
[00:03:34] Callum Reid: Thanks, stores Jamie.
[00:03:37] Jamie Brennan: That's me. Less glamorous than it sounds.
[00:03:41] Marcus Hale: Depends how you feel about cardboard.
[00:03:44] Jamie Brennan: Strong opinions, actually.
[00:03:46] Callum Reid: Right, that's the lot from me. Anything else for this stand-up?
[00:03:52] Priya Raman: Nothing else from me.
[00:03:54] David Whitfield: No, all good.
[00:03:56] Sarah Okafor: Only that the cake isn't going to survive eight people knowing about it.
[00:04:01] Callum Reid: Well, now we know what everyone's thinking about. Cheers, everyone.
[00:04:06] Marcus Hale: Cheers, see you in a bit.

component_mention.description: Equipment exactly as people referred to it; resolve 'it'. Null if none.

site_mention.description: Off-site location, as said. Null if none.

due_mention.description: Deadline words as spoken. Null if none.

due_date.description: Deadline as YYYY-MM-DD using the meeting date and the date rules. Null if none.

priority_mention.description: Urgency words as spoken. Null if none.

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-04-27 (Monday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Aisha Begum, Jamie Brennan, Fiona Doyle, Tomasz Nowak, Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Olumide Adeyemi

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Monday the twenty-seventh. Have we all got sound?

[00:00:18] Callum Reid: Greenhouse. Came in with a coat on, nearly passed out.

[00:00:28] Olumide Adeyemi: Hang on, am I coming through? Teams had the wrong microphone again.

[00:01:41] Marcus Hale: Yeah, the purchase order. That's what I'm chasing today.

[00:01:50] Marcus Hale: Yep, got it.

[00:01:57] Marcus Hale: Favouritism, obviously.
[00:02:00] Sarah Okafor: Absolutely. Right, more seriously, the near miss at the Boiler Safety Relief Valve needs writing up.
[00:02:06] Tomasz Nowak: I'll write up the near miss at the Boiler Safety Relief Valve. That's holding production up so it needs doing first.
[00:02:14] Callum Reid: Yeah, that's the one holding us. Agreed, first.
[00:02:18] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Tomasz. You take the write-up, first priority.
[00:02:23] Tomasz Nowak: Yep. I'll do that first.
[00:02:27] Aisha Begum: Mm. Not something we want half a description of, either.
[00:02:31] Sarah Okafor: Quite. What else, Marcus?
[00:02:33] Marcus Hale: I'll book a contractor to look at the desiccant unit by next Tuesday. No rush on that one.

[00:02:46] Marcus Hale: Making the booking by next Tuesday. I'm not saying they'll be on site that day.
[00:02:54] Sarah Okafor: Fine, Marcus, that's yours. No rush, booking by next Tuesday.
[00:02:57] Marcus Hale: Yep, that's what I meant.
[00:03:01] Jamie Brennan: Fair question. Those two dates get muddled quite easily.

[00:03:14] Aisha Begum: Um, no, sorry. I haven't got the capacity to take that on.
[00:03:20] Sarah Okafor: All right. Doyler, can you take the investigation instead? Same deadline, on Friday, low priority.
[00:03:27] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, I'll take it. I'll investigate the pressure drop on the boiler feed pump, due on Friday. Low priority, understood.
[00:03:36] Aisha Begum: Cheers. Better than me saying yes and sitting on it.
[00:03:40] Fiona Doyle: No, that's fine. I've got room for that.
[00:03:44] Sarah Okafor: Thanks. That goes to Doyler, then.
[00:03:48] Olumide Adeyemi: Sorry, I talked over the end there. Nothing to add, just saying I heard.
[00:03:54] Sarah Okafor: No worries. Everyone clear on the order? The near-miss write-up comes first.
[00:03:59] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, clear.
[00:04:03] Callum Reid: And I've got the parts collection today. All good.
[00:04:08] Sarah Okafor: Anything we've missed before we finish?
[00:04:11] Jamie Brennan: Nothing else from stores.
[00:04:15] Olumide Adeyemi: Nothing from me.
[00:04:17] Aisha Begum: No, I'm good.
[00:04:18] Fiona Doyle: Same here.
[00:04:20] Marcus Hale: All good. Enjoy the tropical portakabin.
[00:04:25] Sarah Okafor: Right, thanks, everyone. Catch you out there.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-04-29 (Wednesday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Aisha Begum, Jamie Brennan, Fiona Doyle, Tomasz Nowak, Callum Reid, Olumide Adeyemi

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Can you hear me all right? Teams has picked a different microphone again.
[00:00:12] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, just about.
[00:00:16] Aisha Begum: Bit faint, Sarah. Sounds like you're at the other end of the room.
[00:00:21] Sarah Okafor: Hang on... there. Headset rather than the laptop.
[00:00:25] Aisha Begum: Yeah, that's better.
[00:00:27] Callum Reid: While we're getting settled, the broken coffee machine in the canteen has really improved my Wednesday.
[00:00:34] Tomasz Nowak: You might have to drink water, Callum. Terrible situation.
[00:00:39] Callum Reid: I've got tea. It's not the same relationship.
[00:00:44] Jamie Brennan: Brought mine from home. Rookie mistake, relying on that thing.
[00:00:49] Fiona Doyle: All right, no need to look quite so pleased with yourself, Jamie.
[00:00:55] Sarah Okafor: Between that and the traffic on the ring road, it's a cheerful start. I barely moved for ages.
[00:01:03] Olumide Adeyemi: Same. Everyone trying the other lane, then trying to get back in.
[00:01:08] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, gaining about half a car length. Anyway, we're here.
[00:01:14] Fiona Doyle: Have we got everyone who's coming?
[00:01:17] Sarah Okafor: Everyone for today, yeah. Haley's not in.
[00:01:21] Sarah Okafor: Haley asked me to pass on where he's got to with chasing the purchase order. He's done the prep; just the write-up left.
[00:01:31] Jamie Brennan: Right, cheers for passing that on.
[00:01:35] Sarah Okafor: Tommo, yours?
[00:01:36] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, the near-miss write-up for the pop valve is finished. All signed off.
[00:01:43] Callum Reid: Good stuff.
[00:01:46] Sarah Okafor: And my contractor booking for the desiccant unit is sorted. They've actually been in as well—no issues found.
[00:01:53] Aisha Begum: Oh, that's reassuring.
[00:01:55] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, nice to have a straightforward one.
[00:01:59] Fiona Doyle: Sarah, what about the timing for sending the shift handover report round?
[00:02:04] Sarah Okafor: That's moved. I'll send the shift handover report round by the end of the week now.
[00:02:12] Fiona Doyle: Right, thanks.
[00:02:16] Sarah Okafor: Okay, today's new bits. Not a massive list.
[00:02:20] Aisha Begum: Go on.
[00:02:22] Sarah Okafor: Tommo, can you grease and check the bearings on the Main Outfeed Conveyor by the 28th? It matters but it's not urgent.
[00:02:30] Tomasz Nowak: Um, I can't take that on, sorry. I haven't got the capacity.
[00:02:36] Sarah Okafor: Fair enough. Olumide Adeyemi, can you take that instead?
[00:02:41] Olumide Adeyemi: The bearings on the Main Outfeed Conveyor, grease and check, yeah?
[00:02:46] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, that's it. By the 28th, and as I say, it matters but it's not urgent.
[00:02:54] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, I'll take it. I'll grease and check the bearings.
[00:02:59] Fiona Doyle: Okay, got that.
[00:03:01] Olumide Adeyemi: Sorry, took me a second. Someone started speaking next to me.
[00:03:05] Tomasz Nowak: Thought you were pretending the connection had gone.
[00:03:10] Olumide Adeyemi: No, no. My frozen face is usually much more convincing.
[00:03:15] Sarah Okafor: Right. Callum, you were coming in there?
[00:03:19] Callum Reid: Yeah, so, the near miss at the new line needs writing up. I'll write that up.
[00:03:26] Aisha Begum: Yeah, that's worth having properly written down.
[00:03:29] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Callum. That's yours, then.
[00:03:33] Callum Reid: Yep, I'll do the write-up.
[00:03:36] Jamie Brennan: Sorry, did I talk over someone then? I got a sort of double voice.
[00:03:42] Aisha Begum: You're all right. We heard Callum.
[00:03:46] Jamie Brennan: Ah, okay. It's doing that thing where everyone goes quiet, then all the sound arrives at once.
[00:03:53] Fiona Doyle: Yes. Usually makes it sound like we're having a much bigger argument than we are.
[00:04:00] Sarah Okafor: Anything else we actually need to agree this morning?
[00:04:05] Tomasz Nowak: Nothing else from me.
[00:04:07] Aisha Begum: No, I'm all right.
[00:04:11] Jamie Brennan: Nothing from stores.
[00:04:14] Olumide Adeyemi: No more here.
[00:04:16] Fiona Doyle: I'm good, thanks.
[00:04:18] Sarah Okafor: Right, we'll leave it there. Thanks, everyone.
[00:04:23] Callum Reid: Cheers. Back to my disappointing tea.
[00:04:27] Sarah Okafor: Enjoy that. Bye, all.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-04-30 (Thursday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Aisha Begum, Fiona Doyle, Tomasz Nowak, Callum Reid, Marcus Hale

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Thursday the thirtieth. Have we got everyone who's in?
[00:00:08] Fiona Doyle: Think so. Tomasz is there, just muted.
[00:00:12] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, I'm here. Headset button and Teams button. Always the wrong one.
[00:00:17] Marcus Hale: We got the sigh before you muted it, mind.
[00:00:21] Tomasz Nowak: That was the chair.
[00:00:25] Sarah Okafor: The furniture, I hope. Jamie Brennan and Olumide Adeyemi are absent today, so it's us six.
[00:00:31] Aisha Begum: Before we start properly, there's a birthday cake in the office. Already cut, if anyone's wondering.
[00:00:38] Callum Reid: That explains the queue past the printer.
[00:00:43] Fiona Doyle: More interest in that than the biscuits, anyway.
[00:00:48] Sarah Okafor: Anything's better than watching the football last night. Honestly, ninety minutes of my life.
[00:00:54] Marcus Hale: You stayed till the end?
[00:00:56] Sarah Okafor: Unfortunately. Right, enough of my poor decisions. Quick updates first.
[00:01:00] Callum Reid: Yeah, go on.
[00:01:03] Sarah Okafor: I can't send the shift handover report round yet. I'm waiting on the permit to be signed, so that's held up.
[00:01:13] Fiona Doyle: Ah, right. Understood.
[00:01:16] Callum Reid: My near-miss write-up at line three is all done. All fine.
[00:01:22] Sarah Okafor: Cheers, Reidy.
[00:01:24] Tomasz Nowak: Sorry, bit of a crackle at my end.
[00:01:28] Marcus Hale: You're clear now.
[00:01:31] Sarah Okafor: And I already swapped the filter on the water ring yesterday. That's sorted.
[00:01:36] Tomasz Nowak: Lovely.
[00:01:38] Aisha Begum: Right, what's new, then?
[00:01:42] Sarah Okafor: I'll go to the hydraulics lot to pick up the replacement parts for the Injection Moulding Line 3 at half two. It matters but it's not urgent.
[00:01:51] Tomasz Nowak: You're collecting them yourself, boss?
[00:01:54] Sarah Okafor: Yep, I'll do the collection.
[00:01:57] Fiona Doyle: Half two is when you're going over, yeah?
[00:02:01] Sarah Okafor: Yeah, at half two. Not a rush trip now.
[00:02:07] Callum Reid: Fair enough. Otherwise everyone hears 'replacement parts' and assumes it's a panic.
[00:02:11] Tomasz Nowak: Usually accompanied by someone standing behind you.
[00:02:16] Sarah Okafor: I feel very seen.
[00:02:19] Aisha Begum: It's the folded arms, boss.
[00:02:22] Sarah Okafor: Right, moving swiftly on.
[00:02:25] Callum Reid: Yeah so, I'll book a contractor to look at the IM2 this morning.
[00:02:31] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Reidy. Whenever you get a chance this morning, no need to drop everything.
[00:02:37] Callum Reid: Yep, that's fine.
[00:02:40] Fiona Doyle: That's the booking this morning, not expecting someone through the gate this morning?
[00:02:45] Callum Reid: Exactly. I'll make the booking. Haven't promised an arrival time.
[00:02:51] Fiona Doyle: Good, that's what I thought you meant.
[00:02:54] Marcus Hale: Contractor teleportation's still a bit unreliable.
[00:02:58] Tomasz Nowak: Especially with the toolbox.
[00:03:00] Fiona Doyle: While we're on timings, I'll schedule downtime for the Engel with production this afternoon. Normal priority.
[00:03:08] Callum Reid: Sorry, Fi, I talked over the end there. You're doing the scheduling this afternoon?
[00:03:14] Fiona Doyle: Yeah. That's when I'll agree the downtime with production, not saying the machine's stopping this afternoon.
[00:03:21] Sarah Okafor: Fine, Fi. Normal priority is right.
[00:03:24] Aisha Begum: Useful distinction. I heard it the other way round for a second.
[00:03:30] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, sorry. First coffee hasn't quite landed.
[00:03:34] Sarah Okafor: One more thing: the monthly fire alarm test needs running at half two. Not an emergency but don't let it slip. Anyone able to take that?
[00:03:45] Marcus Hale: Um...
[00:03:47] Callum Reid: I can't take that one.
[00:03:50] Tomasz Nowak: Nor me, I'm afraid.
[00:03:52] Fiona Doyle: Sorry, no.
[00:03:56] Aisha Begum: I can't commit to that.
[00:03:59] Marcus Hale: No, sorry, neither can I.
[00:04:01] Sarah Okafor: Right. I can't cover it with the collection either. No owner for the fire alarm test, then; it still needs doing at half two.
[00:04:10] Callum Reid: Yeah. Not an ideal clash.
[00:04:13] Sarah Okafor: No. Okay, that's where we are. Thanks, everyone.
[00:04:16] Tomasz Nowak: Cheers.
[00:04:19] Marcus Hale: See you in a bit.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Jamie Brennan, Fiona Doyle, Tomasz Nowak, Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Olumide Adeyemi

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Friday, first of May. Aisha Begum's absent today, so it's just us. Can everyone hear?
[00:00:11] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, bit tinny, but you're there.
[00:00:15] Olumide Adeyemi: Morning. The heating in the portakabin's apparently decided it's December.
[00:00:19] Jamie Brennan: You've still got your fleece on.
[00:00:23] Olumide Adeyemi: It's practically welded to me. Just an observation, before anyone gives me a thermostat to fix.
[00:00:31] Callum Reid: We can hear the fan more than we can hear you.

[00:00:41] Olumide Adeyemi: And the charity bake sale on Friday — today, obviously. I've been thinking it's Thursday all morning.
[00:00:49] Fiona Doyle: That's a dangerous mistake on a Friday.
[00:00:54] Jamie Brennan: Depends whether there's any cake left by the time stores get there.
[00:00:59] Tomasz Nowak: Not with this lot.
[00:01:01] Sarah Okafor: Right, before this becomes a cake allocation meeting. Updates first. Marcus?
[00:01:07] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'm here. Teams was hiding the unmute button from me.
[00:01:13] Marcus Hale: The purchase order chase — my deadline's moved. It's now by the 28th.
[00:01:19] Sarah Okafor: Okay, got that.
[00:01:22] Marcus Hale: And, um, the other one isn't such good news.
[00:01:26] Marcus Hale: I can't get the training records for the new starters sorted because the parts haven't turned up. That's what's holding me up.
[00:01:35] Jamie Brennan: Ah, right.
[00:01:38] Marcus Hale: Bit frustrating, to be honest.
[00:01:41] Sarah Okafor: Yeah. Thanks. Controls next?
[00:01:44] Olumide Adeyemi: Yep, just finding my bit of paper. Very advanced system here.

[00:01:55] Tomasz Nowak: Nice when it's boring.
[00:01:57] Olumide Adeyemi: Boring's absolutely fine with me.
[00:02:00] Sarah Okafor: Jamie, anything to pass on before we get into today's stuff?
[00:02:04] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, passing this on for boss: the run to Kestrel for the replacement parts is done. All picked up.
[00:02:12] Sarah Okafor: Cheers.
[00:02:14] Callum Reid: Am I next, or—
[00:02:16] Fiona Doyle: Go on. Sorry, talked over you.
[00:02:20] Callum Reid: No, you're all right.
[00:02:23] Callum Reid: Booking a contractor to look at line two — I'm about halfway through that. Made some headway, but I haven't got the booking nailed down yet.
[00:02:32] Sarah Okafor: Understood.
[00:02:34] Callum Reid: And I signed off the inspection on the 11kV board on Tuesday. That's already finished.
[00:02:41] Sarah Okafor: Thanks. Doyler?
[00:02:43] Fiona Doyle: The downtime for the Engel is all scheduled with production. That's sorted, no issues found with the arrangement.
[00:02:50] Tomasz Nowak: That sounded remarkably painless.
[00:02:54] Fiona Doyle: Don't sound so surprised.
[00:02:56] Sarah Okafor: Right, today's new bits, then.
[00:02:58] Fiona Doyle: I'll update the risk assessment for work on the Arburg. Normal priority, and I'll have it done by the 28th.
[00:03:06] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Doyler. Agreed on that.
[00:03:09] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, okay.
[00:03:10] Olumide Adeyemi: I've got one as well. Um— sorry, thought someone else was speaking.
[00:03:15] Olumide Adeyemi: I'll write up the near miss at line 2 for next Tuesday. That's fairly important.
[00:03:22] Sarah Okafor: Agreed. Olumide Adeyemi on the write-up, then.
[00:03:26] Olumide Adeyemi: Yep, that's mine.
[00:03:29] Callum Reid: Sorry, your audio clipped at the end there.
[00:03:34] Olumide Adeyemi: Just said yep, that's mine. This microphone's having a morning.
[00:03:38] Sarah Okafor: Olumide Adeyemi, can you do the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the guard switch on two for Monday as well? Drop everything for that one.
[00:03:48] Olumide Adeyemi: No, sorry, I can't take that on for Monday. I haven't got the capacity to commit to it.
[00:03:56] Sarah Okafor: Right, Jamie, can you take the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the guard switch on two instead? Monday, and drop everything for that one.
[00:04:06] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, I'll take that. Lock-out tag-out sign-off on the guard switch on two, Monday. That gets first call.
[00:04:13] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Jamie.
[00:04:16] Tomasz Nowak: Glad you said no rather than just squeezing another thing in.
[00:04:21] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah. Tempting to say yes when everyone's looking at you, isn't it.

[00:04:33] Sarah Okafor: Right, that's the lot. Thanks, everyone.
[00:04:37] Callum Reid: Cheers, all.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Bank holiday or not, here we are. Can you all hear me?
[00:00:11] Callum Reid: Yeah, unfortunately. Had all these weekend plans, barbecue, bit of gardening. Weather had other ideas.
[00:00:17] Fiona Doyle: You didn't actually get the barbecue out?
[00:00:21] Callum Reid: Got as far as taking the cover off. Put it straight back on. Very productive weekend.
[00:00:27] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Meanwhile the heating in the portakabin thinks it's December. I'm sitting here with the door open.
[00:00:35] Marcus Hale: So that's where all the heat's going. Certainly isn't reaching my end.
[00:00:40] Olumide Adeyemi: Morning—sorry, Teams picked the wrong microphone again. Am I coming through now?
[00:00:45] Sarah Okafor: Yep, you're fine now. Bit echoey, but fine.
[00:00:49] Tomasz Nowak: Better than mine. I've got about three people coming out of one little speaker.
[00:00:54] Sarah Okafor: Right. Aisha Begum and Jamie Brennan aren't with us today. We've got everyone else, so let's crack on.
[00:01:02] Fiona Doyle: Yep, I'm here. Calendar's open, coffee's mostly working.
[00:01:07] Sarah Okafor: First, I'm not sending that shift handover report round after all. The other shift already sorted it, so there's no point duplicating it.
[00:01:16] Marcus Hale: Fair enough. One copy's plenty.
[00:01:19] Marcus Hale: And, um, the new starters' training records—I've got the first half done. There's a fair bit left in the second half.
[00:01:28] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, those folders are thicker than they look.
[00:01:32] Callum Reid: My contractor booking for the Arburg is stuck. Waiting on the permit to be signed; I can't get any further with it until that's through.
[00:01:42] Sarah Okafor: Understood. That's the hold-up, then.
[00:01:45] Olumide Adeyemi: The near-miss write-up for the Arburg is finished, though. All signed off.
[00:01:50] Tomasz Nowak: Ah, good. Cheers.
[00:01:51] Olumide Adeyemi: And that monthly fire alarm test we had sitting without an owner—I'll take it on. Put Mide against that one.
[00:01:59] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, that's agreed.
[00:02:02] Sarah Okafor: Doyler asked me to pass on that the risk assessment update for work on the Injection Moulding Line 2 needs to move off her list. Reidy, can you take that over?
[00:02:15] Callum Reid: Yeah, I'll take over the risk assessment update.
[00:02:20] Fiona Doyle: Cheers, appreciate that.
[00:02:22] Fiona Doyle: Oh, and I tested the turbine one gas valve yesterday. It's all fine now, that's sorted.
[00:02:30] Marcus Hale: Good news. Nice to hear something behaved itself.
[00:02:35] Sarah Okafor: Right, onto the new bits. What have we got?
[00:02:39] Tomasz Nowak: I'll check the guarding on the stacker next week. Normal priority, that one.
[00:02:46] Sarah Okafor: Thanks, Tomasz Nowak. Guarding check on the stacker, next week, normal priority. Agreed.
[00:02:52] Tomasz Nowak: Yep. Nothing more urgent than that being suggested.
[00:02:55] Callum Reid: Yeah, that's sensible.
[00:02:57] Sarah Okafor: Tomasz Nowak, can you organise the toolbox talk for the team first thing tomorrow as well?
[00:03:04] Tomasz Nowak: Sorry, no, I can't take organising that on. I haven't got the capacity for it.
[00:03:11] Sarah Okafor: Okay. Doyler, can you take that instead—organise the toolbox talk for the team, first thing tomorrow?
[00:03:19] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, I'll organise it. First thing tomorrow, understood.
[00:03:24] Sarah Okafor: Thanks. That's with you, then.
[00:03:28] Fiona Doyle: Always nice getting the one where everyone looks thrilled to be there.
[00:03:33] Callum Reid: That's just my face before breakfast, to be fair.
[00:03:39] Sarah Okafor: Tom, can you swap the filter on the Line 1 Hydraulic Power Unit by end of day? That one's safety critical, straight away.
[00:03:48] Tomasz Nowak: Right, so that's an immediate start, not something to leave until the end of the shift?
[00:03:56] Sarah Okafor: Exactly. Straight away, with the filter swapped by end of day.
[00:04:01] Tomasz Nowak: Understood. I'll swap the filter on the Line 1 Hydraulic Power Unit. Straight away, done by end of day.
[00:04:09] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, safety critical takes it out of the ordinary queue.
[00:04:13] Tomasz Nowak: Absolutely. No argument from me.
[00:04:17] Sarah Okafor: And Tommo, can you go to the treatment plant to pick up the replacement parts for the main water valve by the 28th? That one's safety critical, straight away.
[00:04:29] Tomasz Nowak: Just checking—you're asking me to collect the parts, not fit them as part of this?
[00:04:34] Sarah Okafor: Correct, collection of the replacement parts. Treat it as safety critical straight away; the collection deadline is by the 28th.
[00:04:42] Tomasz Nowak: Yep, I'll go to the treatment plant and pick up the replacement parts for the main water valve by the 28th. Safety critical, straight away—got it.
[00:04:53] Fiona Doyle: Three versions of your name this morning. Teams will think we've got a bigger maintenance department.
[00:05:01] Tomasz Nowak: Same bloke, sadly. Same pair of hands.
[00:05:06] Sarah Okafor: Quite. Everyone clear on what's been agreed?
[00:05:09] Marcus Hale: Yep, clear from me.
[00:05:13] Olumide Adeyemi: All clear here too.
[00:05:16] Callum Reid: Yeah. And the sun's come out now we're all indoors. Typical.
[00:05:22] Sarah Okafor: Of course it has. Right, thanks everyone. That's us.
[00:05:27] Fiona Doyle: Cheers, all.

traces.name: link_tasks
traces.instructions:
You link jobs extracted from a factory stand-up to the company's master data.

For each task you get the words people used and a shortlist of candidate ids.
- Pick the candidate that the words refer to, using the task wording as context.
- For equipment, if you cannot tell which specific part is meant, pick its parent asset id.
- Return null if none of the candidates fits. Never invent ids.
- Attendee ids are more likely owners than non-attendees.
- category and priority: follow the business rubric below exactly.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

priority.description: 1, 2 or 3 per the priority rubric; 2 if no urgency was expressed

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.
