traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-05-05 (Tuesday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Aisha Begum, Fiona Doyle, Tomasz Nowak, Callum Reid, Marcus Hale, Olumide Adeyemi

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. Bit of a short week, then. Can everyone hear me?
[00:00:07] Tomasz Nowak: Yeah, but there's two of you. One's quite enough.
[00:00:11] Marcus Hale: That's my end, sorry. Teams and the laptop speaker.
[00:00:16] Marcus Hale: There. Headset's actually connected now.
[00:00:18] Sarah Okafor: Lovely. Jamie Brennan's absent today. Otherwise I think we're all here.
[00:00:22] Callum Reid: Yep, I'm here. Camera's off, but I'm here.
[00:00:26] Sarah Okafor: Right, updates first, then a few new bits. How are you getting on?
[00:00:31] Callum Reid: Yeah so, booking the contractor for the Arburg — done the prep, just the write-up left on that.
[00:00:39] Sarah Okafor: Okay, cheers.
[00:00:42] Callum Reid: And the risk assessment for work, I've got the prep done there as well. Just the write-up left. Bit of a theme, unfortunately.
[00:00:51] Fiona Doyle: The paperwork always outlasts the interesting bit.
[00:00:55] Sarah Okafor: Doesn't it just. Tommo?
[00:00:59] Tomasz Nowak: I've made a start on checking the guarding on the stacker. Only partway through it.
[00:01:05] Tomasz Nowak: And that filter swap, I've had a first look. Nothing major so far.
[00:01:11] Sarah Okafor: Right, thanks. Olumide?
[00:01:13] Olumide Adeyemi: Monthly fire alarm test's all done. All fine.
[00:01:17] Callum Reid: Nice. That's what you want to hear.
[00:01:21] Sarah Okafor: Also, Haley asked me to pass on that the new starters' training records need to come off his list. Olumide, I'm moving those over to you to sort.
[00:01:33] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, I'll take over sorting the training records for the new starters.
[00:01:38] Marcus Hale: Thanks, mate. Appreciate that.
[00:01:40] Sarah Okafor: Okay. New bits for today, then.
[00:01:45] Sarah Okafor: Aisha Begum, can you order spare parts for the outfeed conveyor on Friday? Normal priority.
[00:01:50] Aisha Begum: Yeah, just checking — order placed on Friday, not parts landed here on Friday?
[00:01:58] Sarah Okafor: That's right, order placed. Not a delivery deadline.
[00:02:01] Aisha Begum: Fine, I'll order the spare parts for the outfeed conveyor on Friday. Normal priority, got it.
[00:02:08] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, makes sense. Order date and delivery date get muddled so easily.
[00:02:12] Sarah Okafor: Marc, can you chase the purchase order for the Boiler Feedwater Pump this morning? That one's fairly important.
[00:02:20] Marcus Hale: Yeah, so chasing the PO, rather than putting another order in.
[00:02:27] Sarah Okafor: Exactly. Just the chase.
[00:02:29] Marcus Hale: Yep, I'll chase the purchase order for the Boiler Feedwater Pump this morning. Understood, fairly important.
[00:02:36] Tomasz Nowak: The glamorous side of engineering, that.
[00:02:40] Marcus Hale: Oh, living the dream. Headset on, purchase order numbers.
[00:02:46] Sarah Okafor: Fiona Doyle, can you write up the near miss at the pick and place on two after lunch?
[00:02:54] Fiona Doyle: Sorry, you clipped a bit there. After lunch?
[00:02:59] Sarah Okafor: Yes, after lunch.
[00:03:02] Fiona Doyle: Right, yes. I'll write up the near miss at the pick and place on two after lunch.
[00:03:11] Callum Reid: You're clear again now, Sarah. It went a bit robotic for a second.
[00:03:16] Sarah Okafor: Good old Teams. Haley, one more for you: can you check the guarding on the door switch on two next Tuesday? Top priority please.
[00:03:26] Marcus Hale: Next Tuesday, yeah? Not this Tuesday?
[00:03:29] Sarah Okafor: Next Tuesday, yes. Top priority please for that check.
[00:03:33] Marcus Hale: Okay, I'll check the guarding on the door switch on two next Tuesday. Got the priority.
[00:03:40] Aisha Begum: Bank holiday's thrown my sense of the week completely.
[00:03:43] Sarah Okafor: Same here. Right, that's the work covered. Anything else before we finish?
[00:03:49] Tomasz Nowak: Only that the charity bake sale on Friday is apparently very competitive this year. Not a work item, just slightly alarming.
[00:03:59] Fiona Doyle: Competitive how? Are people measuring the cakes?
[00:04:04] Tomasz Nowak: Wouldn't surprise me. Mine would fail the visual inspection.
[00:04:09] Callum Reid: Never mind visual. What's the hardness reading?
[00:04:13] Olumide Adeyemi: Sorry, talking over you — I was going to say, depends whether it's cake or a test piece.
[00:04:20] Marcus Hale: With his baking, both.
[00:04:22] Sarah Okafor: Right, before this turns into a materials review...
[00:04:26] Aisha Begum: Strong start to a Tuesday. We've already got cake tolerances.
[00:04:31] Tomasz Nowak: Cruel, this team. Absolutely cruel.
[00:04:35] Sarah Okafor: And on that note, thanks everyone. We'll leave it there.
[00:04:39] Fiona Doyle: Cheers, all.
[00:04:42] Marcus Hale: Cheers.
[00:04:45] Olumide Adeyemi: Thanks, bye.

traces.name: board_pick
traces.instructions:
You match things said at a factory stand-up to the cards on the team's task board.

For each mention you get only the cards it could be about: the person's open cards and cards on the
same equipment. Pick the card that is the SAME JOB, or "none".
- Same person or same equipment but a different job is not a match.
- A mention said as "new" matches only when it is clearly the same job said again.
- A remark about work that is not on any of its cards is "none".
- People use nicknames for equipment and colleagues.
- Give the reason first: one short sentence on why that card is the same job, or why none of them is.

traces.name: standup_mentions
traces.instructions:
You extract every job mention from a factory morning stand-up transcript for a task board.

The board already holds jobs from earlier stand-ups, so people talk about NEW jobs and give UPDATES on
existing ones. Return one record per job mentioned, with `said`:
- new: a job agreed, asked for or needing doing (even with no owner yet)
- progress: someone worked on it but it is still open
- done: it is finished
- blocked: it cannot go on right now (put the reason in note)
- cancelled: it is not going to happen any more (put why in note)
- reassigned: it moves to someone else, or someone picks up an unowned job (set new_owner_mention)
- due_changed: a new deadline was given for an existing job (set due_mention)

Do NOT extract chit-chat or observations with no action ("it ran a bit warm but settled").
A remark that something is finished is `done` even if you do not know which job it was.
A job first raised in THIS meeting is always `new`, even if it is handed from one person to another or
someone declines it before another accepts ("Dave, can you...?" "Can't, I'm tied up." "Marc, take it?").
`reassigned`, `blocked` and the other update labels are only for jobs from earlier stand-ups.

Rules:
- One record per job per thing said. Merge the ask and the acceptance of the same new job into one record.
- If a job is handed from one person to another, the owner is whoever finally accepted it.
- speaker: the display name of whoever said it, exactly as in the transcript.
- Copy mentions verbatim; do not "correct" nicknames. Leave fields null when not said. Never guess.
- Date rules (relative to the meeting date): "today"/"this afternoon"/"end of day" = meeting date;
  "tomorrow" = +1 day; a bare weekday = its next occurrence after today; "next <weekday>" =
  that weekday in the following Monday-Sunday week; "end of the week" = this Friday;
  "next week" = next Monday; "the 3rd" = next occurrence of that day of month.
  Times: "half two" = 14:30, bare 1-6 o'clock = afternoon.

Business rubric.
category (by the purpose of the job):
  - operations: Running, maintaining, inspecting or repairing plant and production equipment.
  - safety: Hazards, permits, isolations, PPE, incidents, near misses, risk assessments and compliance checks.
  - organisation: Scheduling, staffing, training, ordering parts, contractors, site visits, paperwork and meetings.
  Safety checks and tests (fire alarm tests, pre-use checks, guarding, lock-out) are safety;
  ordering, booking, scheduling, chasing, visits and paperwork are organisation.
priority (only from what was said about urgency):
  - 1: Urgent. Must happen today or is safety-critical or stops production.
  - 2: Normal. Should happen this week.
  - 3: Low. Nice to have, whenever there is time.
  If nobody said anything about urgency, priority is 2. "Not an emergency but don't let it slip" is 2.

Meeting date: 2026-05-06 (Wednesday)
Attendees: Sarah Okafor, Aisha Begum, Jamie Brennan, Fiona Doyle, Tomasz Nowak, Marcus Hale, Olumide Adeyemi

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Sarah Okafor: Morning, everyone. You all there? Teams is showing me about three different versions of who's joined.
[00:00:09] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, I'm here. Yours froze for a second, but we can hear you.
[00:00:14] Tomasz Nowak: Same here. Just getting the headset straight.
[00:00:19] Jamie Brennan: I'm here, without coffee. The broken coffee machine in the canteen has really improved the atmosphere this morning.
[00:00:27] Aisha Begum: Oh, the broken coffee machine in the canteen got me as well. Stood there pressing the button like it might change its mind.
[00:00:36] Marcus Hale: Persistence. That's engineering, that is.
[00:00:41] Olumide Adeyemi: Depends how many times you pressed it.
[00:00:45] Sarah Okafor: Right, before we get the full fault history of that—Callum Reid's absent today. Let's have the updates first. Mide?
[00:00:54] Olumide Adeyemi: Yeah, so, the training records for the new starters. I've had a first look through; nothing major so far. A fair bit of paperwork to get through, though.
[00:01:05] Sarah Okafor: Okay, thanks.
[00:01:07] Jamie Brennan: Can I jump in? I've got mine and a quick one from Tommo.
[00:01:12] Sarah Okafor: Yep, go on, stores Jamie.
[00:01:14] Jamie Brennan: I've made a start on the lock-out tag-out sign-off for the door switch on two. That's as far as I've got with it.
[00:01:25] Jamie Brennan: And Tommo asked me to pass on that the guarding check on the stacker is all done. We weren't sure his headset was going to cooperate.
[00:01:35] Tomasz Nowak: Cheers. Yeah, it picked a good moment to come back.
[00:01:39] Fiona Doyle: The toolbox talk for the team is all organised now, from my side. No issues found with any of that.
[00:01:48] Sarah Okafor: Lovely, thanks, Fiona Doyle.
[00:01:51] Tomasz Nowak: And I've finished the filter swap on the power pack on one. That's sorted.
[00:01:56] Aisha Begum: While we're on filters, I already swapped the filter on the pump in the pit yesterday. All done.
[00:02:05] Jamie Brennan: You looked like you'd been down a mine when you came back.
[00:02:10] Aisha Begum: It wasn't my finest look, no.
[00:02:14] Sarah Okafor: Doyler, was there anything else on yours?
[00:02:19] Fiona Doyle: Yeah, the near-miss write-up for the arm on two—I'm not doing that now. The supplier's doing it under warranty instead, so ours is cancelled.
[00:02:28] Sarah Okafor: Right, understood.
[00:02:31] Fiona Doyle: That's everything from the earlier stuff.
[00:02:34] Jamie Brennan: Just an observation from me: I saw the pressure on the CT1 dip for a few minutes. It came back on its own.
[00:02:44] Sarah Okafor: Without anyone touching anything?
[00:02:46] Jamie Brennan: Yeah, no intervention. Back where it was. Just mentioning what I saw, really.
[00:02:51] Olumide Adeyemi: Mm, okay. A brief dip, then.
[00:02:54] Sarah Okafor: Thanks. Right, new work—Haley?
[00:02:56] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'll replace the seals on the gas valve on one by the end of the week.
[00:03:04] Sarah Okafor: Okay, Haley, agreed. The seals on the gas valve on one are yours.
[00:03:11] Marcus Hale: Yep, I'll take that.
[00:03:14] Tomasz Nowak: Always sounds like a tiny job when you just say 'seals', doesn't it?
[00:03:21] Marcus Hale: Yeah, well, I'm not saying it's a five-minute one.
[00:03:24] Fiona Doyle: End of the week, then. Got that.
[00:03:28] Sarah Okafor: Good. What else have we got?
[00:03:33] Aisha Begum: I'll do a site visit at the hydraulics lot with the contractor tomorrow. Low priority, that one.
[00:03:39] Sarah Okafor: Yep, Aisha, agreed. Low priority.
[00:03:43] Aisha Begum: Yeah. A visit with them, that's all I'm putting forward.
[00:03:47] Fiona Doyle: Tomorrow, Thursday. Sorry, my head was still on Tuesday for a moment.
[00:03:53] Aisha Begum: Definitely tomorrow. This week's doing that to me as well.
[00:03:59] Sarah Okafor: Right, Aisha has the hydraulics lot visit with the contractor tomorrow.
[00:04:04] Jamie Brennan: Sorry, was that me dropping out or did everyone get the robot voice?
[00:04:10] Olumide Adeyemi: Just you, I think. Sounded normal here.
[00:04:15] Jamie Brennan: Ah, okay. Back now.
[00:04:18] Sarah Okafor: Anything else new that needs agreeing?
[00:04:21] Tomasz Nowak: Nothing else from me.
[00:04:23] Olumide Adeyemi: No, that's me.
[00:04:25] Fiona Doyle: Nothing further here.
[00:04:27] Marcus Hale: Nope, all covered.
[00:04:31] Jamie Brennan: Only my coffee grievance, and that's not a maintenance request.
[00:04:36] Aisha Begum: Good, because I think we've given it enough airtime.
[00:04:39] Sarah Okafor: We have. Right, thanks everyone. That's us.
[00:04:44] Fiona Doyle: Cheers, all.
[00:04:47] Tomasz Nowak: Cheers.
